title: China-to-Canada Industrial Motor Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Covered product class — three-phase industrial AC motors
rows.target_requirement: Canada treats many three-phase industrial AC motors as regulated products for energy efficiency and as electrical equipment requiring acceptable Canadian certification for installation and sale. The practical target profile is a motor suitable for Canadian 60 Hz service and common 600/347 V industrial distribution, with Canadian evidence for safety and efficiency.
target_standards: CSA C22.2 motor safety certification pathway
rows.china_equivalent: China's common industrial motor baseline is GB 18613 for IE efficiency classes, aligned with IEC 60034-30-1, plus GB 12665 for cooling and CCC where a below-1 kV motor falls within the CCC catalogue scope.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: A China-market motor classification does not prove the motor is in the Canadian regulated class, certified for Canadian electrical installation, or suitable for 60 Hz / 600 V service. Product selection must be re-mapped to Canadian scope, voltage, frequency, and certification rules.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the motor is covered by Canadian electrical approval and NRCan regulated-product rules
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where GB 18613, GB 12665, or CCC catalogue rules apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Classify the motor against Canadian regulated-product and electrical-equipment rules before relying on a China GB or CCC file. The 60 Hz / 600 V design basis is a core Canada-market qualification check.

rows.requirement: System design class — 60 Hz and 600/347 V industrial service
rows.target_requirement: Canadian industrial installations commonly use 60 Hz supply and 600/347 V three-phase distribution. A motor for Canada should be rated, tested, nameplated, and protected for the actual Canadian supply system, including starting current, thermal rise, speed, torque, insulation, and protection-device coordination at 60 Hz.
rows.china_equivalent: China-market industrial motors are commonly designed around 50 Hz and 380 V three-phase service, with GB 18613 efficiency classification, GB 12665 cooling requirements, and CCC where the motor is within scope.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The 60 Hz versus 50 Hz and 600 V versus 380 V mismatch is a prominent technical gap. Reusing a China 50 Hz / 380 V design can change speed, torque, losses, heating, insulation stress, and protection settings, and may invalidate safety and efficiency evidence.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory in practice for safe Canadian installation and certification acceptance
mandatory_status.cn: Common domestic design baseline, not a Canada-market acceptance basis

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat frequency and voltage as design gates, not minor label changes. A Canada-bound motor should be engineered and documented for 60 Hz and the applicable Canadian voltage system before CSA or NRCan evidence is finalized.

rows.requirement: NRCan minimum efficiency — IE3 for covered motors
rows.target_requirement: Natural Resources Canada regulates covered electric motors under Canadian energy-efficiency rules. Covered motors must meet mandatory minimum energy performance requirements that are commonly expressed as IE3 / premium-efficiency level for relevant industrial motor classes.
target_standards: NRCan electric motor energy efficiency requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China GB 18613 defines IE-aligned motor efficiency classes, with GB 12665 for cooling and CCC where below-1 kV motors fall in CCC scope. GB 18613 evidence may show an IE class but does not itself establish Canadian regulatory compliance.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: A Chinese IE3 claim is not enough by itself. The motor must be within or outside Canadian scope based on Canadian definitions, and covered motors need NRCan-acceptable efficiency evidence for the rated Canadian frequency and voltage configuration.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm Canadian scope first, then document IE3 or higher performance using NRCan-acceptable evidence. CCC or GB 18613 documents alone do not replace Canadian energy-efficiency compliance.

rows.requirement: CSA C390 test evidence for motor efficiency
rows.target_requirement: Canadian motor efficiency evidence commonly relies on CSA C390 methods for energy performance testing and reporting. Test data should correspond to the motor configuration sold into Canada, including 60 Hz operation and the applicable Canadian voltage rating.
rows.china_equivalent: China efficiency testing is normally tied to GB 18613 and related Chinese test methods, with GB 12665 for cooling and CCC where applicable. These documents may be useful engineering inputs but are not automatically Canadian test evidence.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: A 50 Hz / 380 V Chinese test report can be misaligned with the Canadian sale configuration. Efficiency, losses, and thermal behavior should be evidenced for 60 Hz and the intended Canadian voltage, or the technical file may not support the Canadian declaration.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory evidence expectation for covered regulated products
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory or supporting evidence depending on Chinese scope and certification path

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build the Canada file around the actual 60 Hz Canadian configuration. Retesting or engineering justification may be needed where the original China report covers only 50 Hz / 380 V operation.

rows.target_requirement: For regulated energy-using products, the Canadian importer or dealer must be able to support compliance with required energy performance information and records before import or sale. Motors that do not meet the Canadian minimum may be blocked from lawful distribution.
target_standards: NRCan import and reporting requirements for regulated energy-using products
rows.china_equivalent: China-market files typically include GB 18613 efficiency classification and CCC documents where applicable to below-1 kV motors in scope. These are domestic compliance records, not Canadian import filings or dealer records.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The gap is procedural as well as technical: Canadian energy records, declarations, and importer controls must be assembled even when the motor already meets a China IE grade.

mandatory_status.cn: Domestic records mandatory where Chinese rules apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not treat China factory certificates as the Canadian energy file. The importer should hold Canada-specific energy evidence and records for the covered motor before import or sale.

rows.requirement: ISED ICES EMC requirements for motor equipment
rows.target_requirement: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada administers EMC and radio-equipment requirements. Motor products with electronic drives, switching controls, or digital components may need evidence against applicable ICES standards for interference-causing equipment, and radio modules require the relevant ISED authorization path.
rows.china_equivalent: China files commonly focus on GB 18613 efficiency, GB 12665 cooling, and CCC where the below-1 kV motor is in scope. EMC reports may exist for controllers or drives, but they are not a substitute for Canadian ISED ICES evidence.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: A bare induction motor may have limited EMC exposure, but a motor-drive package can be interference-causing equipment. Canada-specific ICES applicability should be checked for the final product configuration, especially for variable-frequency drives and smart controls.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where ICES or radio rules apply
mandatory_status.cn: Depends on Chinese EMC or CCC scope for the product configuration

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Check ISED ICES exposure at the motor-package level, not only the motor core. Drives, electronic starters, sensors, and wireless modules can trigger Canadian EMC or radio obligations.

source.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

rows.target_requirement: If the motor assembly includes a variable-frequency drive, connected controller, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cellular, or other radio transmitter, the final Canadian product may need ISED radio certification or use of approved radio modules in addition to ICES EMC evidence.
target_standards: ISED Certification and Engineering Bureau requirements
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese motor compliance is typically anchored in GB 18613, GB 12665, and CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope. China radio or EMC approvals for a connected controller do not automatically transfer to ISED authorization.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The final Canadian configuration may differ from the base motor tested in China. Adding a VFD, wireless module, or smart controller can create a separate Canadian EMC or radio-compliance workstream.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where radio transmitters or interference-causing equipment are present
mandatory_status.cn: Depends on product configuration and Chinese approval scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat connected or VFD motor packages as a different compliance object from a bare motor. ISED obligations should be checked after the final controller and radio configuration is frozen.

source.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

rows.requirement: CSA certification for Canadian market access
rows.target_requirement: Industrial motors placed into Canadian installations typically need certification by CSA Group or another certification body acceptable in Canada, with markings and documentation recognized by provincial and territorial electrical authorities. Canadian safety acceptance is separate from energy-efficiency compliance.
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic evidence usually includes GB 18613 efficiency, GB 12665 cooling, and CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope. CCC is a China compulsory certification system and is not recognized as Canadian CSA certification.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: CCC is not recognized for Canada. A motor that is legal for China sale still needs Canadian certification evidence and marking before it can be accepted for Canadian installation or distribution.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for accepted Canadian electrical installation and market access
mandatory_status.cn: CCC mandatory only where the China catalogue applies

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Plan a Canadian certification route rather than relying on CCC. CSA-recognized safety evidence and Canadian marking are core import-readiness items for industrial motors.

rows.requirement: NRCan import compliance for covered motors
rows.target_requirement: Canada requires regulated energy-using products, including covered motors, to meet the applicable efficiency standard before import or interprovincial shipment. Importers must maintain and provide required energy-efficiency information when applicable.
rows.china_equivalent: China GB 18613 documents show domestic efficiency class alignment, and CCC documents may apply for below-1 kV motors in scope. These are not NRCan import records or Canadian dealer compliance files.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: Import readiness requires Canada-specific energy documentation. Chinese domestic conformity evidence may be part of the engineering file, but it does not replace the Canadian importer or dealer obligations.

mandatory_status.cn: Domestic conformity required only under Chinese scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] The Canadian importer should confirm scope, retain efficiency records, and ensure the motor meets Canadian minimum efficiency before import. China-only paperwork is not enough.

rows.requirement: Nameplate, labeling, and bilingual market documentation
rows.target_requirement: Canada-market motors should have nameplate and documentation aligned to the certified Canadian ratings, including frequency, voltage, phase, efficiency, certification mark, and installation information. Depending on sale channel and province, English and French documentation may be expected for market use.
target_standards: Canadian consumer and language rules where applicable
rows.china_equivalent: China nameplates commonly reflect GB 18613 efficiency class, GB 12665-linked technical assumptions, Chinese domestic voltage and frequency, and CCC marking if the below-1 kV motor is in CCC scope.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: A 50 Hz / 380 V China nameplate is a red flag for Canada. The Canadian label must match the 60 Hz and applicable Canadian voltage rating, with CSA and NRCan evidence aligned to the same configuration.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where certification, energy information, or language rules apply
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory domestic markings where Chinese rules apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not relabel a China 50 Hz / 380 V motor as Canada-ready unless the underlying design, test file, and certification all support the Canadian rating. Documentation should be built around the certified Canadian configuration.

rows.target_requirement: Industrial motors used in Canada need Canadian electrical safety acceptance, commonly through CSA certification or an equivalent certification body accepted by Canadian authorities. Evaluation should cover insulation, temperature rise, enclosure, grounding, terminals, markings, and use at the certified Canadian voltage and frequency.
rows.china_equivalent: China baseline documents may include GB 18613 efficiency, GB 12665 cooling, and CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope. These do not prove Canadian electrical safety acceptance or provincial installation approval.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The safety gap is structural: Canada does not accept CCC as a substitute for CSA-type certification. Testing and marking must be tied to the Canadian rating, including 60 Hz and 600 V where applicable.

mandatory_status.cn: CCC mandatory only where China scope applies

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Obtain Canadian electrical safety certification for the actual Canada-bound motor configuration. CCC, GB, or factory QA documents cannot replace CSA-accepted evidence.

rows.target_requirement: Environment and Climate Change Canada administers substance and environmental controls that can affect motor materials, coatings, insulation systems, oils, packaging, and restricted substances. Exporters should screen the bill of materials and safety data sheets for Canadian environmental restrictions before shipment.
target_standards: Prohibition of Certain Toxic Substances Regulations where applicable
rows.china_equivalent: China motor files commonly focus on GB 18613 efficiency, GB 12665 cooling, and CCC where below-1 kV motors are in scope. These files usually do not establish Canadian environmental or restricted-substance compliance.
china_standards: CCC for below-1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: CSA and NRCan files do not automatically close ECCC substance questions. Material declarations, SDS review, and restricted-substance screening should be added for Canada-bound motors and accessories.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where Canadian substance or environmental controls apply
mandatory_status.cn: Depends on Chinese chemical, product, and CCC scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Add ECCC screening to the Canada export checklist. Motors with compliant safety and efficiency files can still have unresolved restricted-substance or environmental documentation gaps.
